steps: A timed-out follower increments its term and requests votes.
A majority elects it leader for term 8.
The leader appends a client command and replicates it to followers.
After majority storage, the commit index advances and state machines apply the entry.

lesson.scenario: A three-node Raft group elects a leader and commits a payment command at log index 9.

steps.title: Follower timeout
steps.narration: N1 times out with all logs committed through index 8.
steps.outcome: The cluster has no active leader after the timeout.
steps.invariant: Terms increase monotonically and identify election epochs.

steps.title: Election starts
steps.narration: N1 increments to term 4, votes for itself, and requests votes.
steps.outcome: N1 has two votes including N2.
steps.invariant: A voter grants at most one vote per term and requires an up-to-date candidate log.

steps.title: Leader appends
steps.narration: N1 becomes leader and appends charge(42) at term 4 index 9.
steps.outcome: The command exists on the leader and N3.
steps.invariant: The leader assigns one term-index position to each new command.

steps.title: Majority replication
steps.narration: N3 acknowledges index 9, giving the leader a majority.
steps.invariant: A leader commits a current-term entry after replication on a majority.

steps.title: Commit propagated
steps.narration: N1 sends the new commit index and N2 catches up.
steps.outcome: All state machines apply the same command at index 9.
steps.invariant: Committed log entries remain in the same position on future leaders.

production.scenario: A service-mesh control plane stores route weights in a Raft cluster so every sidecar proxy in a multi-AZ Kubernetes fleet consumes one coherent desired state during canary rollout.
components: Lets traffic engineers change the canary weight for the checkout service
Validates xDS route updates and owns rollout history
Commits one ordered config log for service-mesh state
Authoritative xDS snapshot revisions for checkout routing
Apply the committed route weights on live request paths
Rebuilds a recovered Raft member from the latest snapshot
flows: The platform engineer submits a new route weight for the checkout deployment.
append route-weight update to config log
The mesh API writes the change through the Raft cluster so there is one ordered history for xDS state.
After the config entry is committed, the desired-state store exposes revision 9812 as the latest authoritative snapshot.
Every checkout sidecar subscribes to the committed revision and updates routing tables in the same order.
The control plane can tell which proxies are already using the new canary weight before continuing the rollout.
If a Raft node is rebuilt in another AZ, the restore worker seeds it from the last snapshot before it starts serving traffic again.
